document.title: Staffdel Focuses on Afghanistan at MFA (Islamabad 04780)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), "No-Go" Tribal Areas Became Basis for Afghan Insurgency Documents Show
document.note: [Sensitive But Unclassified] Less than two weeks before 9/11, U.S. congressional staff meet Pakistani Foreign Ministry officials. The Pakistanis say they "don't support, but inter-act with the Taliban" and deny that ISI or the government arms the Taliban. They recommend engagement, saying Taliban obscurantism, not Pashtun tribalism, drives the war, and suggest corrupting the Taliban with aid and a reborn economy.

events.description: HIRC staffers Berkowitz and Adams met Pakistani MFA officials on Afghanistan, Indo-Pak and US-Pak issues.
Consular access granted by Taliban for Western SNI detainees, after Pakistani pressure.
HIRC staffers Paul Berkowitz and David Adams met Pakistani MFA officials in Islamabad on Afghanistan, Taliban engagement, SNI detainees, sanctions and democratization.
U.S. Embassy Islamabad cabled the staffdel meeting report to the State Department (cable 04780).
The Taliban granted consular access to the detained Western SNI aid workers after Pakistani pressure; press speculated they would be released soon.
Deadline pledged by Musharraf for party-based elections in Pakistan.

key_claims: Pakistani MFA officials defended engagement with the Taliban as pragmatic and consistent with dealing with whoever rules Kabul since 1947.
A Pakistani official denied that ISI or any part of the GOP arms or militarily assists the Taliban.
Pakistan claimed access to Taliban leaders but said Afghans make their own decisions.
Pakistani official argued Taliban rule roughly 90 percent of Afghanistan and the Northern Alliance would collapse without external support.
Pakistan urged the US to keep open channels to the Taliban and to lift Pressler, Symington and Glenn sanctions on Pakistan.
